title: Minimum Detectable Misalignment: What Is the Sensitivity of Current Alignment Evaluations?
original_idea: Induce emergent misalignment at multiple sub-threshold doses. Administer standard alignment probes at each dose. Compute the minimum induction dose at which probes reliably detect misalignment (power analysis style). Compare across multiple probe suites.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: evaluation sensitivity unknown -> low-level misalignment goes undetected -> false confidence in deployment safety. Characterizing sensitivity directly enables informed deployment decisions. Each link is explicit.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Misalignment induction at varying doses follows established protocols. Running probe suites is standard evaluation. Power analysis is a well-documented statistical method. Intermediate complexity accessible to CS students with stats background.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused first deliverable: one model, one induction method, vary dose, one probe suite, compute detection threshold. The dose-response curve with detection threshold is a clean, self-contained result achievable within 30 hours.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
